# Shailaputri v0 — anomaly detection on real metric series

Trained and tested on **NAB (real series only)** (numenta/NAB @ `ea702d75cc22`), 47 series in 5 families. Each family is held out in turn; the threshold is chosen on the training families only. Every detector is scored online by the same harness (`pashupatastra.evaluation.evaluate`) on exactly the same series.

Recall is per anomaly *episode*; false alarms are per 1000 judged points; lead is how many points before the window's end the first flag came (higher is earlier).

## Mean across held-out families

| Detector | F1 | Precision | Episode recall | False alarms / 1000 | Lead |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| EWMA | 0.261 | 0.185 | 0.900 | 14.2 | 229.0 |

| seasonal-robust-z | 0.312 | 0.220 | 0.761 | 74.7 | 241.3 |

## How to read this

- A detector that flags everything catches every episode and drowns the operator; read F1 with false alarms per 1000, never alone.
- NAB's labels are windows around each anomaly, and Wu & Keogh (2021) show several NAB series are trivial or mislabelled — results here inherit those limits.
- Designed, written and trained by an AI assistant under the owner's direction ([adr/RealDataModels](../../adr/RealDataModels.md)).
